title: Preparation and hydrogen storage capacity of templated and activated carbons nanocast from commercially available zeolitic imidazolate framework
material_description: BF-900 | ZIF-templated carbon nanocast from commercial ZIF-8 (Basolite Z1200, Sigma-Aldrich) template: furfuryl alcohol impregnation, heating at 80 C (24 h) then 150 C (6 h) under Ar, carbonization under Ar at 900 C for 8 h (ramp 3 C/min); ZIF template removed during carbonization; not activated
source_location: main-5 (J. Mater. Chem. p.150), Fig. 6a, series BF-900 (green down-triangles), marker at 1.53 bar
notes: archive: Fig6a_BF-900.json; marker centre px (704.8, 1313.0), 4 px; plot does not distinguish adsorption and desorption points; all markers coded adsorption (paper: isotherms completely reversible, no hysteresis). Temperature printed as -196 C (liquid nitrogen bath). BET range: 0.06-0.22. Surface area: BET from N2 sorption at -196 C (Micromeritics ASAP 2020); micropore surface area and micropore volume (Table 1 values in parentheses) given without stated method; total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/P0 = 0.99. Basis: paper does not name excess/absolute/total; IGA gravimetric with stated density inputs for the wt% calculation (quote: 'The hydrogen uptake in wt% was calculated on the basis of a density of 1.5 g cm-3 for the carbon samples and a density of 0.04 g cm-3 for the hydrogen'), read as a buoyancy correction, hence basis_inferred = excess by the instrumental default; skeletal_density_g_cm3 = 1.5 is this assumed carbon density, not a measured He density. IGA manufacturer/model not named. Degas before H2: oven-dried 24 h at 80 C, then 200 C and 10^-10 bar (stored as 1e-05 Pa) for 4-6 h (duration printed as a range; field left empty). NLDFT pore size maxima 8/15/20 A (Table 1); not stored as an average pore diameter. Table 1 H2 uptake density 13.9 umol H2 m-2 (uptake per surface area at 20 bar, computed by the paper; not stored as areal uptake). Residual Zn from incomplete template removal: TGA residual mass at 1000 C ca. 11.5 wt% (Fig. 2 text), attributed to Zn; Zn content itself not stated, residual_metal_wt_pct left empty. Kept as templated_carbon (residual template, not an added non-carbon phase). isotherm_point_count = markers countable on Fig. 6a; markers in the unresolved low-pressure pile (below ca. 1-1.5 bar) could not be counted, so the true count is larger.

activation_method: KOH activation: carbon/KOH weight ratio 1/4 (KOH/carbon 4), 700 C for 1 h under N2 flow, ramp 3 C/min; washed three times with 2 M HCl then distilled water to neutral pH; dried at 120 C for 3 h
source_location: main-5 (J. Mater. Chem. p.150), Fig. 6b, series ACBF-1100 (black crosses), marker at 14.02 bar
notes: archive: Fig6b_ACBF-1100.json; marker centre px (1071.0, 1287.7), 3 px; black crosses isolated on a derived copy of the page image in which saturated pixels (max-min >= 45) were set to white; geometry unchanged; plot does not distinguish adsorption and desorption points; all markers coded adsorption (paper: isotherms completely reversible, no hysteresis). Temperature printed as -196 C (liquid nitrogen bath). BET range: 0.06-0.22. Surface area: BET from N2 sorption at -196 C (Micromeritics ASAP 2020); micropore surface area and micropore volume (Table 1 values in parentheses) given without stated method; total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/P0 = 0.99. Basis: paper does not name excess/absolute/total; IGA gravimetric with stated density inputs for the wt% calculation (quote: 'The hydrogen uptake in wt% was calculated on the basis of a density of 1.5 g cm-3 for the carbon samples and a density of 0.04 g cm-3 for the hydrogen'), read as a buoyancy correction, hence basis_inferred = excess by the instrumental default; skeletal_density_g_cm3 = 1.5 is this assumed carbon density, not a measured He density. IGA manufacturer/model not named. Degas before H2: oven-dried 24 h at 80 C, then 200 C and 10^-10 bar (stored as 1e-05 Pa) for 4-6 h (duration printed as a range; field left empty). NLDFT pore size maxima 8/13/21 A (Table 1); not stored as an average pore diameter. Table 1 H2 uptake density 15.4 umol H2 m-2 (uptake per surface area at 20 bar, computed by the paper; not stored as areal uptake). isotherm_point_count = markers countable on Fig. 6b; markers in the unresolved low-pressure pile (below ca. 1-1.5 bar) could not be counted, so the true count is larger.
